items.statement: The review identified practical arguments based on definition, convenience, calculation, and comparability, together with theoretical arguments about scale anchoring and QALY properties.
An additive change to the origin of the duration scale did not preserve indifference between the hypothetical health episodes, but a positive multiplicative transformation preserved it.

items.statement: Under the stated QALY assumptions and zero conditions, a duration of zero years has value zero and dead has health-utility value zero.
The position of dead relative to other health states changes the weight given to life-saving and life-improving treatments and determines which health states receive negative values.
source: Full article, The Position of Dead Relative to Other Health States

items.statement: The authors conclude that both the duration scale and the health-utility scale must have ratio-scale properties and that dead must be assigned the value zero.
The authors conclude that the relative position of dead must be established carefully because it affects cost-utility decisions and separates positive from negative health states.
The authors state that measurement methods which compare health states with dead should receive more attention.
Potentially relevant information might not have appeared in the titles and abstracts used during electronic-literature screening, so full-text searching could have found more information.
source: Full article, Limitations and Strengths, first paragraph
